claim: The canonical dated-append shapes (retirement stamp, used-to-be clause, date-stamped parenthetical) mark accreted narrative in a present-tense artifact, and a deterministic checker over them is composable by the parent's probe
method: quorum signature gate — review by 1 reader(s), quorum 1; verdict = the reviewers', seal recorded by notary 'CC' (same hand, under ruling '2026-09-05-cc-may-sign-concept-pieces-this-session')

signatures.restated: Read and restated: a dated append is a shape that narrates a change instead of stating the current design, so the artifact carries two tenses at once and the reader re-derives the settled (Law 1). Three canonical shapes are named with pattern, example and why-it-signals: RETIRED (a succession narrated where only the successor should stand), 'formerly' (provenance in a present-tense hat), and a date-stamped parenthetical (the commonest — a dated note appended instead of a rewrite). The checker is deterministic Python, owned by this child and composed by the parent probe at cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/probes/present_tense_artifacts_carry_no_dated_appends.py. A legitimate dated append is handled as a labeled exception, never by loosening a pattern.

delegation.now_the_spec_says: For the session of 2026-09-05, CC holds the reviewer's seat on concept-pieces: CC may sign AND seal, and the seal door records that as a same-hand seal under this ruling, never as different hands.

falsifier: a present-tense artifact that must legitimately carry a dated append with no labeled-exception mechanism — or a corpus specimen of accreted narrative that none of the three shapes matches
horizon: until the parent probe's enough-count (10 clean charter writes) clears the watch, or a fourth canonical shape is measured in the corpus
